title: Impulsive Pressurization of Neuronal Cells for Traumatic Brain Injury Study
protocol: Seed SH-SY5Y human neuroblastoma cells at a density of 3×10^3 cells/cm² using growth media composed of DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
Culture cells on 18 mm diameter glass coverslips in a 5% CO₂ humidified incubator at 37°C.
Treat cells with media further supplemented with 10 μM retinoic acid (RA) for neuronal differentiation, changing the medium every two days.
On day 7 of RA treatment, cells are ready to be pressurized.
Suspend two aluminum alloy bars by aligned brass bearings for the Kolsky bar setup.
Position and engage a friction clamp on the incident bar for pulse duration control.
Pre-compress the clamp-mass section of the incident bar using a scissors jack.
Release pre-stored compression in the incident bar rapidly to generate a pressure pulse with a hydraulic system.
Propagate the generated pressure pulse through the incident bar toward the test chamber piston.
Pressurize fluid and cells within the pressurization chamber impulsively due to the propagating pulse.
Initiate a pressure pulse propagation in the transmitted bar downstream from the chamber.
Sterilize all pressurization chamber parts using the autoclave.
Keep sterilized chamber parts under UV light.
Assemble the chamber inside the cell culture hood.
Loosely engage the vent screw in the air vent at the base of the cavity.
Pipette pre-warmed (37°C) fresh growth media into the chamber without making bubbles.
Pick up a cell-cultured glass slide and place it on the cap of the piston with cells facing outside.
Tighten small holding screws down onto the slide to hold it in place.
Insert the piston with the cell-cultured glass slide a little into the cavity of the chamber.
Tilt the assembly with the vent being at the highest point.
Remove the vent screw.
Push the piston into the cavity, forcing out air bubbles and then excess fluid.
Use either a reference mark or a jig as a guide to ensure consistent media volume for every test.
Sanitize the vent screw.
Replace the vent screw to make the chamber water tight.
Reset the Kolsky bar system by moving the heavy mass back to its original position.
Replace the used locking bolt with a new one.
Engage the new locking bolt with the hydraulics to about 200 psi.
Use the scissors jack to compress the pre-loading section of the incident bar up to a pressure slightly higher than the desired value.
Back off the jack to engage the full friction of the jack's screw.
The data acquisition is now armed.
Mount the assembled cell pressurization chamber into the system.
Place the chamber in a V block supported by small lab scissors jack and align with two bars.
Grease each interface with a light grease layer.
Rub butting surfaces together to eliminate air gaps.
Force the clamp locking bolt to break by quickly pumping the hydraulic clamp driver.
Separate the clamp and observe data acquisition results.
Determine cell pressurization history from measurements of transmitted bar gauge.
Remove the cell pressurization chamber after testing.
Disassemble the chamber inside the cell culture hood.
Remove the vent screw.
Pull the piston free of the chamber.
Take out the cell-cultured glass slide from the end of the piston.
Inspect cells immediately after pressurization.
Incubate cells further if examination is delayed.
Use aseptic operation processes for long-term incubation.
Examine pressurized cells using molecular and cellular biology techniques.
Assess pressure-induced changes in neurite outgrowth in neuronal cells.
Evaluate microtubule cytoskeletal changes in neuronal cells.
Investigate neuronal gene expression alterations due to pressure.
Measure apoptosis levels in neuronal cells under pressure conditions.
Use non-pressurized cells as control samples for comparison.
Examine pressurized and chamber control cells by optical microscope immediately after pressurization and 1 and 24 h post-incubation.
Fix cells with a 4% w/v paraformaldehyde solution.
Rinse fixed cells with a 0.05% v/v Tween-20 wash buffer.
Permeabilize cells with a 0.1% v/v Triton X-100 solution.
Block cells with a 1% w/v bovine serum albumin solution.
Incubate cells with tetramethylrhodamine isothiocyanate (TRITC)-conjugated phalloidin.
Take immunofluorescent images of the cells using a fluorescent microscope.
Quantify lengths of neurites for pressurized and control cells using ImageJ software.
Identify neurites as axons or dendrites.
Fix cells after 0 and 24 h post-pressurization.
Stain fixed cells with β-tubulin antibody.
Observe stained cells by fluorescent microscope.
Extract total RNA from pressurized and control cells.
Perform quantitative RT-PCR or real-time RT-PCR to examine gene expression.
Seal the chamber using a method that involves taping the piston with Teflon plumber's tape to reduce friction and prevent gouging.
Move the cell-containing chamber under sterile conditions when transitioning between the Kolsky bar, pressurization setup, and cell culture hood.
Sterilize all chamber parts before use to maintain sterility during handling and experiments.
Assemble and disassemble the cell-cultured slide and chamber inside a cell culture hood to ensure sterility.
Allow for post-incubation times of up to several weeks under sterile conditions for long-term studies.
Record the pressure profile obtained from each pressurization event for data analysis.
Manually exclude cell response data that corresponds to unwanted pressure profiles during data analysis.
Assemble the chamber for the Kolsky bar setup.
Transfer and mount the assembled chamber into the Kolsky bar.
Pressurize the chamber to the desired pressure level.
Transfer the pressurized chamber back to its original position.
Disassemble the chamber after pressurization.
Prepare the next cell culture slide immediately after disassembly.
Repeat the entire process for subsequent experiments as needed.
Use 18 mm diameter glass coverslips for each experiment setup.
Conduct three repeated pressurization experiments to gather sufficient protein amount for western immunoblotting.
